description: Viklund & Wang showed Loewner energy equals Dirichlet energy dissipation under conformal welding. The Loewner energy of the boundary of an extremal Bloch domain quantifies its 'complexity'. Minimizing Loewner energy over domains achieving a given covering radius could yield new lower bounds or structural constraints on extremal functions.
mathematical_formalization: For a Jordan curve Γ, the Loewner energy is I_L(Γ) = ∫_0^∞ |λ̇(t)|^2 dt where λ is the driving function. For f univalent with f'(0)=1, B_u ≥ inf{B_f : I_L(∂f(D)) < ∞}.
implementation_hypothesis: Discretize the Loewner equation. For candidate boundary curves, compute driving function via zipper algorithm. Evaluate Loewner energy and search for curves minimizing energy subject to covering constraint.
experiment_seed: Implement zipper algorithm. For star-shaped domains with varying boundary cusps, compute Loewner energy vs. maximal inscribed disk radius. Plot Pareto frontier.
